lead.title: Multiwave wins FDA clearance for its AI-powered ultra-low-field portable brain MRI
lead.deck: The Geneva medtech has secured FDA 510(k) clearance for MGNTQv0, a brain MRI weighing just over 250 kg that plugs into a wall outlet, needs no cooling or magnetic shielding, and targets a cost 5-10x lower than conventional MRI; a US commercial launch on a subscription model is planned for 2027 from its Lowell, Massachusetts subsidiary. The company says it is the first portable MRI from Europe to clear the FDA — a young startup (CHF 3.6M raised in 2025) now preparing its CE mark and, logically, a larger round.

milestone.title: MMI adds monopolar energy to its Symani microsurgery robot and performs first cases in Europe
milestone.summary: The NanoWrist Monopolar Scissors, CE-marked in October, add electrical dissection and bleeding control to the Symani robot; first uses at Bellvitge Hospital (Spain, two lymphovenous bypasses in a breast cancer patient with lymphedema) and RWTH Aachen University (head and neck tumor resection). The instrument is still 510(k) pending in the US.
milestone.why: Robotic microsurgery is moving from suturing alone to a full platform that can dissect and coagulate: that broadens indications (reconstruction, lymphedema, ENT) and makes the robot more profitable for hospitals — a textbook case for a medtech born near Pisa.

deal.thesis: Led by Miles Ahead with Wit-Gele Kruis (a home nursing network that is also a partner), the imec.istart Fund and business angels, the round funds regulatory work (from CE Class I to MDR Class IIa), R&D and commercial growth in equal parts. Thesis: a purely software sensor — the camera — that measures blood pressure, HRV and stress in 30 seconds becomes a reusable building block, from telecare apps to humanoid robots.

brefsEurope.title: IntelliProve raises €2.7M seed to pursue MDR Class IIa for its face-scan health check
brefsEurope.summary: The Belgian startup, already CE-marked Class I for its signal acquisition engine, measures biomarkers (blood pressure, heart rate variability, stress) from a 30-second face scan; the round was led by Miles Ahead, with Wit-Gele Kruis and the imec.istart Fund.

brefsEurope.title: Clarity Sensors wins €2.2M NIHR award for low-cost photon-counting CT detectors
brefsEurope.summary: A 2022 University of Cambridge spin-out, Clarity Sensors leads the three-year PICASO project with the STFC Technology Department to make photon-counting CT more affordable using perovskite semiconductors; the project will also assess its clinical and economic impact for the NHS.

brefsIntl.title: Zimmer Biomet files a 510(k) for the autonomous version of its Monogram orthopedic robot
brefsIntl.summary: A hands-free, foot-pedal-activated version compatible with CT imaging, for total knee replacement; Zimmer is targeting clearance in 2027, a year ahead of its original plan. Comparable: robotic autonomy is entering the standard regulatory pathway.

brefsIntl.title: J&J installs its first commercial Ottava robot at Memorial Hermann in Houston
brefsIntl.summary: Granted De Novo authorization in July for ten upper-abdominal procedures, Ottava builds its four arms into the operating table; first installation through the early access program. A market signal for European robotics players (CMR, Distalmotion) facing Hugo and da Vinci.

brefsIntl.title: Exo receives $11.6M from the Gates Foundation to expand access to portable ultrasound
brefsIntl.summary: The grant targets low- and middle-income countries, where nearly two-thirds of people lack reliable access to ultrasound according to the World Bank; it confirms funders' appetite for point-of-care imaging, the same segment portable MRI is chasing.

word.definition: An MRI that runs on a magnetic field tens of times weaker than a hospital scanner (a few tens of millitesla instead of 1.5 to 3 tesla), making it light and frugal enough to be wheeled to the patient's bedside.

parts.label: Low-field permanent magnet
parts.role: the magnetic field, with no helium or cooling

parts.label: AI reconstruction
parts.role: the denoising that makes the image readable

how.t: A compact magnet aligns the protons in the body's water; at low field, the resonance frequency drops and the collected signal is much weaker.
Radiofrequency coils excite and then listen to those protons; the machine plugs into a standard outlet and tolerates metal implants better.
AI and advanced reconstruction algorithms offset the low signal-to-noise ratio to produce a clinically usable brain image.

word.why: Conventional MRI costs millions and needs a shielded room: ultra-low field promises bedside MRI (stroke, ICU, emerging markets) on a subscription model. Multiwave's FDA clearance, after Hyperfine's Swoop, shows the regulatory path is open; the VC question is now clinical proof versus CT and the business model.

startups.name: Multiwave
startups.use: MGNTQv0 AI-powered ultra-low-field portable brain MRI; FDA 510(k) in November 2026, US launch planned for 2027

startups.name: Chipiron

startups.name: Hyperfine
startups.use: Swoop, the first FDA-cleared portable low-field brain MRI; next generation launched in Europe in 2026 (CE/UKCA)

startups.name: Promaxo
startups.use: Office-based low-field MRI (58–74 mT) to guide prostate biopsies, 510(k)-cleared
